chunks: 2559 - Al-Ḥalabī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله enter iḥrām at night or during the day?” So he said:
“During the day.” I said: “At what time?” He said: “At the time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer).”

Then I asked him: “When do you think we should enter iḥrām?” He said: “It is the same for you. The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered iḥrām at the time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer) only because water was scarce; it used to be found on the tops of the mountains. A man would go out early toward such a place the next day, and they would hardly be able to obtain water. These waters have only recently come into existence.”

key_terms.أُحْدِثَتْ: was newly introduced or made available
key_terms.رُءُوسِ ٱلْجِبَالِ: the tops of the mountains, where water used to be found
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْكُمْ: it is the same for you; there is latitude
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءَ: water, mentioned as a practical factor in the ruling context

ai.seo_question: When should one enter iḥrām according to the hadith of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the time at which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entered iḥrām, stating that it was during the day at the time of the ẓuhr salat (prayer). The Imam عليه السلام explains that this timing was connected to historical conditions of water scarcity, indicating flexibility for others rather than an absolute requirement to follow that exact hour.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2559 - Al-Halabi asked Abu Abdullah (as):
"Did the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) enter the state of Ihram at night or during the day?"
Imam (as) replied: "During the day."
I asked: "At what time?"
Imam (as) said: "At the time of the Zuhr prayer."
I then asked him: "When do you think we should enter Ihram?"
Imam (as) said: "It is the same for you. The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) entered Ihram at the time of the Zuhr prayer because water was scarce and was only found at the tops of the mountains. A man would set out in the afternoon and find himself in a similar situation the next day, struggling to find water. These water sources have only been made available recently."
